<Link id="#details" />


## Description



Function comparators in µTest++ provide a clear and expressive way to compare actual and expected values within test cases. While any expression yielding a boolean value may be used in expectations and assumptions, dedicated comparator functions such as <code>eq</code>, <code>ne</code>, <code>lt</code>, <code>le</code>, <code>gt</code>, and <code>ge</code> offer enhanced reporting by explicitly showing the values involved when a check fails.



Using these comparators ensures that, in the event of a failed check, the test output will include both the actual and expected values, making it easier to diagnose issues and understand the cause of the failure.



Comparators are available for both fundamental types and standard containers. When comparing containers, each element is assessed individually, and the results are reported in detail.




<SectionUser title="Examples">

</SectionUser>


<ProgramListing extension="cpp">

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::eq (compute&#95;answer (), 42)) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is 42&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::ne (compute&#95;answer (), 43)) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is not 43&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::lt (compute&#95;answer (), 43)) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is &lt; 43&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::le (compute&#95;answer (), 43)) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is &lt;= 42&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::gt (compute&#95;answer (), 41)) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is &gt; 43&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::ge (compute&#95;answer (), 42)) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is &gt;= 42&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (compute&#95;condition ()) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;condition is true&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>



If a comparator check fails, the output will clearly indicate the actual and expected values:




<ProgramListing extension="console">

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  Check failed comparisons</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">    ✗ actual != 42 FAILED (unit-test.cpp:286, 42 != 42)</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">    ✗ FAILED (unit-test.cpp:307, 42 != 42)</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">    ✗ 42 != 42&#95;i FAILED (unit-test.cpp:310, 42 != 42)</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">    ✗ (actual == 42) and (actual != 42.0) FAILED (unit-test.cpp:781, (42 == 42</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">and 42 != 42.000000))</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>




### Comparing containers



Containers can be compared for equality or inequality using the same comparator functions. The comparison is performed by iterating through each element and evaluating them individually.




<SectionUser title="Examples">

</SectionUser>


<ProgramListing extension="cpp">

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::eq (std::vector&lt;int&gt;&#123; 1, 2 &#125;, std::vector&lt;int&gt;&#123; 1, 2 &#125;))</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">        &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;vector&#123; 1, 2 &#125; eq vector&#123; 1, 2 &#125;&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::ne (std::vector&lt;int&gt;&#123; 1, 2, 3 &#125;, std::vector&lt;int&gt;&#123; 1, 2, 4 &#125;)</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">        &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;vector&#123; 1, 2, 3 &#125; ne vector&#123; 1, 2, 4 &#125;&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>
